This class is modeled as either a specifically dependent continuant or a process profile to align with SSN/SOSA’s treatment of properties that may be continuant features or features of processes, both of which can be the target of intentional change.

Actuation is modeled as a planned process because it is intentionally carried out according to a procedure in order to change the state of the world, which aligns directly with the CCO notion of a PlannedAct.

ObservableProperty mirrors ActuatableProperty in being modeled as either a specifically dependent continuant or a process profile, reflecting that observable aspects may be features of continuants or temporally extended features of processes.

sosa:Observation is modeled as a cco:PlannedAct with internal structure because it involves intentional acts of observation and measurement carried out according to a procedure. The cco:has_process_part restriction captures the necessary internal structure without overcommitting to an equivalentTo axiom, since observations may have additional process parts.

sosa:Platform is modeled as a bfo:MaterialEntity defined by its role in hosting systems, without committing to parthood, attachment, or containment as necessary conditions. The equivalentTo axiom captures that hosting at least one system is both necessary and sufficient for being a platform.
Result is allowed to be either informational or material because SOSA results include both informational outputs (e.g., measurements) and material outputs (e.g., samples).
Sample is modeled as a material entity because it is a physical thing intentionally produced or selected to stand in for a feature of interest.

sosa:Sampling is modeled as a cco:PlannedAct because it is intentionally carried out according to a procedure to create or transform samples. The equivalentTo axiom captures that being prescribed by a procedure and producing a sample as output is both necessary and sufficient for being a sampling.

Accuracy is modeled as a function rather than a quality because it concerns how well a system performs relative to truth conditions when realized in processes. The use of measurement information entities reflects that accuracy is assessed through evaluative measurement, not directly observed as an intrinsic quality.

This is mapped as a specifically dependent continuant or process profile because conditions are not standalone entities but aspects of a system or its operation that depend on something else and characterize circumstances under which performance is evaluated. The link to PerformanceSpecification reflects that conditions are specified and constrained rather than independently realized.

DetectionLimit is modeled as a function because it characterizes the system’s ability to distinguish presence or absence under uncertainty when realized in processes. The reliance on veracity measurement reflects that detection limits are probabilistic performance characteristics rather than simple qualities.

Drift is modeled as a function because it concerns systematic behavior over time that is manifested through processes rather than existing as a static property. The realization through deviation measurement reflects that drift is assessed by analyzing changes relative to expected values.

Frequency is modeled as a function because it constrains how often a system can perform actions when realized in planned acts. Treating frequency as an occurrent part of realizations reflects that it is manifested through repeated execution rather than existing independently.

Latency is modeled as a function because it characterizes temporal performance behavior that is only manifested when the system operates. The cause–effect structure and temporal region reflect that latency is measured through realized processes rather than inherent qualities.

MaintenanceSchedule is modeled as a disposition because it represents a tendency or requirement for maintenance to occur under certain conditions. Its realization through maintenance acts reflects that the schedule itself is not a process but is realized in processes.

OperatingPowerRange is modeled as a function because it constrains operational capability with respect to power when realized in processes. Power appears as an occurrent part of realizations rather than as an independent entity.

OperatingProperty is modeled as a specifically dependent continuant or process profile because it characterizes how a system operates under given conditions without being a realizable capability. Its prescription by design reflects engineering intent rather than measured performance.

OperatingRange is modeled as a specifically dependent continuant or process profile because it describes permissible conditions for normal operation rather than behavior itself. The link to ArtifactDesign reflects that operating ranges are design-specified constraints.

Precision is modeled as a function because it concerns consistency across repeated realizations of system behavior. The reliance on reliability measurement reflects that precision is assessed statistically across processes, not as a single intrinsic property.

Resolution is modeled as a function because it characterizes the system’s capacity to discriminate differences when realized in operational processes. The use of deviation measurement reflects that resolution is evaluated by analyzing minimal detectable change through realized behavior.

ResponseTime is modeled as a function because it characterizes temporal system behavior that emerges during operation. The realization via cause–effect process structure reflects that response time is only meaningful when the system is acting.

Selectivity is modeled as a function because it describes how a system behaves during operation with respect to isolating intended properties. The realization in planned acts reflects that selectivity is manifested through operational behavior involving participants.

Sensitivity is modeled as a function because it concerns proportional relationships between input changes and output changes when realized in processes. The ratio-based measurement reflects that sensitivity is an evaluative performance characteristic, not a basic quality.

SurvivalProperty is modeled as a function because it concerns the system’s capacity to remain viable over time under conditions. The affordance-based realization reflects that survival characteristics emerge from design-enabled processes.

SystemCapability is modeled as a specifically dependent continuant or process profile because capabilities are dependent characteristics of a system that describe what it can do, not processes themselves. The use of PerformanceSpecification captures that capabilities are defined relative to stated performance criteria and conditions.

SystemLifetime is modeled as a function because it characterizes the extent of operational viability rather than a static attribute. Its realization in stasis of operationality reflects that lifetime is manifested as sustained functioning over time.

ssn:Deployment is modeled as a cco:PlannedAct because it involves intentional positioning or installation of systems for a purpose, rather than constituting a structural relation such as parthood. The equivalentTo axiom captures that deploying at least one system on at least one material entity is both necessary and sufficient for being a deployment.
Input is mapped to InformationContentEntity because SSN inputs are informational resources made available to procedures, not material participants or process parts.
Output is modeled as an information content entity because SSN outputs are informational artifacts produced by executing procedures, regardless of whether they later influence material processes.

ssn:Property is modeled as the union of bfo:SpecificallyDependentContinuant and bfo:ProcessProfile in order to accommodate both intrinsic qualities that inhere in independent continuants and temporal properties that are process profiles of occurrents within a single SOSA abstraction.

The retained mapping characterizes Stimulus as a CCO Cause that is the cause of some Observation. The historical rationale treats a stimulus as an event or happening that causally contributes to an observation and expressly selects necessary-and-sufficient equivalence for this characterization.

ssn:System is modeled as a bfo:MaterialEntity defined by its capability to implement procedures. The equivalentTo axiom captures that being a material entity that implements at least one procedure is both necessary and sufficient for being a system, reflecting the functional rather than structural definition in SOSA.

sosa:Actuator is a bfo:MaterialEntity because actuators are physical devices. The bfo:RealizableEntity it bears is realized in actuation processes, capturing the functional rather than purely structural definition of actuators. The cco:agent_in restriction captures that the actuator plays a causative role in the actuation.

`sosa:hasSample` relates a Feature of Interest to a Sample used to represent it. No direct BFO/CCO mapping is adopted.

The reviewed direct candidates do not preserve the source meaning generally:

- Mapping to CCO `represented by` would treat the Sample endpoint as representational information content, which does not capture physical specimens, sampling locations, and other material Samples generally.
- Mapping to BFO `generically depends on` would assign the generically-dependent-content role to the sampled Feature of Interest rather than capturing samplehood.
- A participation mapping also does not represent the relation between a sampled feature and its sample.

Historical work proposed the composite representation path:

represented_by(feature, information-content)
AND
generically_depends_on(information-content, sample)
→
hasSample(feature, sample)

This path should NOT be reinstated as an unconditional formal mapping.

It is not sufficient for samplehood: an ordinary representational carrier such as a book, photograph, recording, or other information-bearing artifact may bear content representing an entity without thereby being a Sample of that entity.

It is also not established as necessary: SOSA's notion of intended representativeness does not by itself require commitment to a distinct CCO information-content entity borne by every Sample.

The previous OWL implementation additionally creates simplicity/profile problems because `hasSample` is inverse-functional and is the inverse of a property used with cardinality/functionality constraints. That implementation issue is secondary to the semantic decision and is NOT the reason for the no-direct outcome.

Accordingly:

No reviewed direct BFO/CCO relation or unconditional BFO/CCO relation chain adequately captures `sosa:hasSample` across its source usage.

This does NOT rule out:
- a future guarded representation rule;
- a query-level mapping;
- a more specialized sample-provenance model;
- weaker documentary correspondences to other vocabularies.

changes.new_value:
`sosa:isSampleOf` relates a Sample to the Feature of Interest that it is intended to be representative of. No direct BFO/CCO mapping is adopted.

The reviewed direct candidates do not preserve the source meaning generally:

- Mapping to CCO `represents` would treat every Sample as representational information content.
- Mapping to BFO `is carrier of` would treat the sampled Feature of Interest as generically dependent content.
- Mapping to participation would confuse the feature being sampled with a process in which the Sample participates.

Historical work proposed:

is_carrier_of(sample, information-content)
AND
represents(information-content, feature)
→
isSampleOf(sample, feature)

This should NOT be reinstated as an unconditional formal mapping.

The representation/carrier path is not sufficient for samplehood. A carrier may bear information representing an entity without being intended or functioning as a Sample of that entity.

It is also not established as necessary. Intended representativeness in SOSA does not by itself require a separately instantiated CCO information-content entity.

Because `isSampleOf` is functional, an overbroad representation-chain mapping would also create undesirable consequences: a carrier bearing representations of multiple distinct entities could infer multiple `isSampleOf` successors and thereby force equality of those represented entities.

The historical OWL chain also creates simplicity/profile conflicts with retained source functionality/cardinality axioms. Again, this is an implementation consequence, not the semantic basis of the no-direct decision.

Accordingly:

No reviewed direct BFO/CCO relation or unconditional BFO/CCO relation chain adequately captures `sosa:isSampleOf` across its source usage.

This does NOT rule out a future more specifically conditioned representation or provenance model.
